evidence_ledger.paper_title: Service screening with mammography in Northern Sweden: effects on breast cancer mortality – an update
evidence_ledger.exact_source_passage: RESULTS: The relative rate (RR) of breast cancer death as excess mortality and UCD for women aged 40-74 years invited to screening, compared with women not yet invited, was 0.70 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.56-0.87) and 0.74 (95% CI 0.62-0.88), respectively.

disagreements.topic_or_metric: Relative mortality reduction (Risk Ratio/Relative Rate) for breast cancer in women aged 40-49
disagreements.plausible_moderator_or_reason: The primary divergence stems from the study design and control group definition. W4248013900 is a systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational data, reporting a pooled relative mortality of 0.76-0.85 with wide confidence intervals that often cross 1.0 (indicating statistical uncertainty/non-significance for the specific 40-49 subgroup in some analyses). In contrast, W2110153513 is a single-center service screening study using a 'women not yet invited' control group, which is susceptible to selection bias and lead-time bias, yielding a more precise and statistically significant reduction (RR 0.70-0.74). Additionally, the Swedish overview in W4248013900 notes faster tumor progression in this age group, which may attenuate the benefit of screening compared to older age groups, whereas the service study may reflect local implementation efficiencies or unmeasured confounders.
disagreements.suggested_follow_up_investigation: Conduct a meta-analysis specifically isolating RCT data for the 40-49 age group to distinguish true biological efficacy from service-based observational biases. Investigate the impact of tumor biology (e.g., proliferation rate, hormone receptor status) in this age group to determine if faster progression negates the lead-time benefit of screening. Compare the 'not yet invited' control methodology in service studies against RCT controls to quantify the magnitude of selection bias in this specific age demographic.
